hero.headline: Vision Marine Technologies to sell Palm City property, consolidates operations
hero.teaser: Vision Marine Technologies has a pending sale of its Palm City property and has consolidated tender-rigging operations at its Fort Lauderdale marina.
hero.body:
Vision Marine Technologies announced the pending sale of its Palm City property. The company has completed consolidating its tender-rigging operations at its Fort Lauderdale marina location.

The consolidation moves tender-rigging work from Palm City to Fort Lauderdale. Vision Marine completed this operational shift as it prepares to sell the Martin County property.

The company announced both the consolidation completion and the pending property sale on Tuesday. The moves represent a restructuring of Vision Marine's Florida operations.

Vision Marine Technologies focuses on marine operations in Florida. The Fort Lauderdale marina location will now serve as the consolidated base for the company's tender-rigging services.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce commissioners reject lawsuit settlement over Little Jim Bait & Tackle waterfront dispute
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer in a lawsuit alleging years of waterfront mismanagement tied to histo.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer in a lawsuit alleging years of waterfront mismanagement tied to historic restaurant Little Jim Bait & Tackle. Plaintiff Kevin Keene said he will continue to pursue litigation against the city following the vote. The city has filed a motion to dismiss Keene's amended complaint. Under the proposed settlement terms, Keene would have dropped the case if the city halted any new plans for Little Jim until Florida Department of Environmental Protection permit issues are resolved and allowed a public vote on future waterfront land decisions. Documents WPTV obtained from the FDEP claim the city has been operating docks on state-owned submerged land at Little Jim without the required permits since 2021. The state agency has ordered the city to pay nearly $16,000 by July 17.

City Commissioner Michael Broderick acknowledged the permit issue and said someone at some point extended the docks further than allowed. He plans to negotiate FDEP's fines down while the city investigates who authorized the extension. The dispute traces back to last year when the Fort Pierce landmark of nearly 80 years faced an uncertain future after its lease expired. Despite five formal proposals submitted to the city, including one from current operators, the city said none met the criteria and scrapped plans to pick a new tenant. Keene argues the Little Jim process was marked by instability, changing information and unresolved material issues, pointing to a broader pattern including Fisherman's Wharf, where state records show the city promised land it didn't own, and King's Landing, where a developer claims the city promised buildable property that contained 1,500 tons of old power plant concrete. The Fisherman's Wharf handling led to a current multi-million dollar lawsuit filed against the city.

cards.headline: Martin County School District cuts 16 administrative positions to save $3.9 million
cards.teaser: The Martin County School District plans to eliminate 16 administrative and district-level positions, including three assistant principal positions, as part of a reorganization for the upcoming school year.
cards.body:
The Martin County School District plans to cut district staff as part of a reorganization for the upcoming school year, saving nearly $4 million from next year's budget. Superintendent Michael Maine told WPTV that the plan includes eliminating 16 administrative and district-level positions, which includes three assistant principal positions and removing 42 unfilled instructional vacancies. Maine said 10 of those vacancies were held in reserve, contingent on increasing enrollment. The reorganization eliminates positions that Maine felt are no longer needed at the district office, allowing the district to absorb a majority of the reduction. The changes are expected to save about $3.9 million from the district's projected budget next school year.

Maine said the cuts reflect how the district routinely manages staffing each year, looking at projected student enrollment and allocating resources accordingly. The Martin County School District currently enrolls 16,000 students. Maine said the goal is to protect classroom resources while streamlining operations at the district level. He emphasized that the district can become more efficient at the district office with taxpayer dollars to be able to do more with less at the district level versus at individual school sites. Maine described his approach to the reorganization as lean and mean.

Not everyone is fully on board with the scope of the cuts. Abigal, whose son will be a fourth grader at Jensen Beach Elementary this fall, said she values the small class sizes and close teacher relationships the district currently offers. She noted that teachers have one-to-one interactions with the kids and do a lot of different kinds of learning. She said she hopes the district is careful about how deep the cuts go.

Abigal expressed concern about maintaining adequate resources for students, saying that children need the administrators, teachers, and all the resources they can get. Maine stated that for a district of Martin County's size, the $3.9 million in savings represents a significant amount of money. He maintained that this approach to staffing represents the normal way the district operates, adjusting positions based on projected student numbers.

cards.headline: Aldi to open first Hobe Sound grocery store Wednesday at former Winn-Dixie site
cards.teaser: Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi store when the new grocery store opens July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road, in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be.
cards.body:
The new Aldi grocery store opens July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be. Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years.

There will be a grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 9 at 8:30 a.m. The first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card. The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.

cards.headline: DeSantis closes final bill-signing season after signing 2,037 laws, reshaping Florida
cards.body:
Ron DeSantis has likely wrapped his final regular bill-signing season, closing one of his last major opportunities to shape Florida law from the governor's desk. With the new fiscal year underway and DeSantis term-limited from seeking another consecutive term, the regular lawmaking window for his administration is essentially closed, barring a future special session, emergency response or other extraordinary action. Florida's Constitution bars a governor who has served more than six years across two consecutive terms from being elected to the succeeding term.

A review of regular-session action shows the scale of DeSantis' eight years in office: 2,037 regular-session bills signed since 2019, along with 66 regular-session vetoes. His busiest year came in 2023, when 341 regular-session bills became law. His lightest was his first year, 2019, with 189. Those laws reshaped major parts of Florida life. Under DeSantis, Florida expanded school choice, with the governor signing HB 1 in 2023 to eliminate income restrictions and open scholarship programs more broadly to students across the state. He also signed new abortion restrictions, including Florida's six-week ban, after first approving a 15-week restriction earlier in his tenure. The list includes permitless carry, expanded immigration enforcement, COVID-era limits on vaccine and mask mandates, new election laws, restrictions on diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and major property insurance changes. DeSantis also signed 2026 legislation giving Florida new authority tied to terrorist organization designations and additional limits on local DEI programs, continuing a broader conservative policy push in his final years in office. That agenda became central to the national brand DeSantis promoted as the Florida blueprint, a fast-moving conservative policy model powered by Republican control of the Legislature and the governor's office.

DeSantis also used his veto power to block dozens of bills. In 2022, he vetoed a net-metering bill that critics said would have hurt rooftop solar customer incentives. That same year, DeSantis vetoed an alimony overhaul, citing concerns about retroactivity. In 2024, he vetoed hemp restrictions, arguing the bill would impose heavy regulatory burdens on small businesses. In 2026, he vetoed a sovereign immunity bill that would have increased lawsuit limits against state and local government entities.

Over eight years, DeSantis vetoed roughly $10.6 billion in spending, using Florida's line-item veto power to cut local projects, trim legislative priorities and reinforce his image as a fiscal conservative. In June, DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year after nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, with his office calling it the fourth straight year of declining state spending. Democrats and local officials have often criticized those cuts, arguing they hit community projects, infrastructure needs and social services. DeSantis and his allies have defended them as necessary discipline in a fast-growing state budget.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie pancreatic cancer patient approved for experimental treatment after 62-day wait
cards.teaser: Russell Reed, a 64-year-old Port St. Lucie man battling pancreatic cancer, received approval to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug, just two days after sharing his story with WPTV.
cards.body:
Russell Reed spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug his oncologist believed could help after traditional treatments were no longer effective. The 64-year-old Port St. Lucie man said chemotherapy was no longer helping him at this point. Daraxonrasib, also known as RMC-6236, is an investigational once-daily oral pill developed by Revolution Medicines. The drug targets mutated KRAS proteins, which drive more than 90% of pancreatic cancers. According to Reed's family, his oncologist submitted a request through the FDA's Expanded Access Program, which can allow patients with serious or life-threatening illnesses to receive treatments outside of clinical trials when other options are limited.

Just two days after sharing their story with WPTV, Reed learned he had been approved to receive the treatment. The drug is now in his hands, and his family says he is already feeling better and optimistic about what comes next. Reed said research and clinical trial results gave him hope that daraxonrasib could help slow the progression of his disease, calling it a miracle drug for pancreatic cancer based on anecdotal evidence and clinical trial data. While daraxonrasib is not considered a cure for pancreatic cancer, the Reeds say the approval represents something they've been fighting for all along: more time together.

cards.headline: Vero Beach homeowner says $9,000 annual insurance costs may force her to sell home
cards.teaser: A Vero Beach homeowner says skyrocketing insurance costs may soon force her out of her home, and her story is one many Florida homeowners know all too well.
cards.body:
Kelly Hagen reached out to share her frustration over the relentless rise in her homeowners insurance premiums. Her home, which has three bedrooms and two baths, is about 1,500 square feet and was built in 1994. Her homeowners insurance is $9,000 a year, which equates to $750 a month on top of her mortgage payment. Her insurance went from $6,000 to $8,000 the next year. Hagen says the financial pressure goes beyond the premium itself. Her insurance company requires impact windows, an expensive upgrade she has struggled to afford while working two jobs. She works a full-time job and then works Instacart nights and weekends. Her situation was made worse when she was turned away for a $10,000 My Safe Florida Home grant after it took too long to find a contractor, a roadblock many Florida homeowners have faced.

State leaders say now is the time for homeowners to shop around, pointing to new insurers entering the market with competitive rates. One new company, Stand Insurance, is offering to help homeowners connect with affordable contractors. Stand uses AI technology to study homes and then works to pair homeowners with vendors and contractors to make repairs. Dan Preston, the CEO of Stand Insurance, said that if you can help someone be safer and have their home be safer, it's beneficial to everyone involved. For Hagen, the window to find a solution is closing fast. She said she can probably hang on just a couple more months, and then she will have to try and sell her house. She said leaving would be devastating.

hero.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in Seattle
hero.body:
The United States men's soccer team saw its World Cup hopes end at home Monday night after losing 4-1 to Belgium at Lumen Field in Seattle. Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal as Belgium exposed American defensive weaknesses to advance to the quarterfinals, where they will face 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco. The loss marked the second time in 12 years that Belgium knocked the United States out in the round of 16, as the Red Devils extended their unbeaten streak to 18 games while seeking their first World Cup title.

Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 in the 31st minute with his second free kick goal of the tournament after Brandon Mechele knocked down Folarin Balogun about 25 yards from goal. Tillman's kick deflected off Hans Vanaken's head to the left of goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois. However, the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff, prompting coach Mauricio Pochettino to show his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying. American star Christian Pulisic injured his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt and was replaced seven minutes later.

De Ketelaere opened the scoring in the eighth minute, marking the first time the United States conceded first in this year's World Cup. Timothy Castagne hooked a centering pass around Chris Richards, and De Ketelaere split Tim Ream and Antonee Robinson to redirect the ball into an open net with his right foot. De Ketelaere scored again in the 33rd minute when he outjumped Ream and headed the ball past goalkeeper Matt Freese. Vanaken added Belgium's third goal in the 57th minute after Freese lost control of the ball in front of his net, and second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku scored the final goal in the third minute of stoppage time after Belgium stripped the ball from Richards.

The Americans played with star forward Balogun, whose one-game red card suspension was controversially lifted by FIFA. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the United States failed to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 in front of a crowd of 66,925. All six CONCACAF nations have been eliminated from the tournament, with co-hosts United States, Mexico and Canada all falling in the round of 16.

cards.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
cards.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
cards.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted images of four syringes on Instagram showing the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena said in an Instagram post that she was heartbroken to withdraw and did everything she could but her knee was not ready to compete.

Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. Venus, who is 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday together with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that was not scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, stating on social media to stay tuned to a city near you. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: President Trump called FIFA president before World Cup suspension of Folarin Balogun was lifted
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American star forward Folarin Balogun, whose red card suspension was lifted before Monday's World Cup match against Belgium.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American star forward Folarin Balogun, whose red-card suspension was lifted in a decision that allows him to play in a World Cup match against Belgium on Monday. Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after Wednesday's game asking FIFA review the red card, according to a person familiar with the call who spoke on condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to speak publicly about the matter. Balogun, the American leader with three goals in the tournament, received a red card for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Tarik Muharemović of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 2-0 round of 32 win, triggering an automatic one-game suspension. FIFA announced Sunday that the suspension had been lifted for the round of 16 match, an extraordinary move that appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup did not result in a suspension. Trump said in a statement on social media thanking FIFA for doing what was right and reversing a great injustice.

The Royal Belgian Football Association said it was astonished, and Belgium coach Rudi Garcia mocked FIFA's action. Garcia compared the decision to April Fools' Day, saying the Belgian federation defends football in general, its integrity and ethics. The Belgian federation said in a statement it was investigating all potential options to safeguard the legitimate rights of all participating teams and protect the fundamental principles of fair play. U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino applauded FIFA's move, stating the team was punished enough against Bosnia-Herzegovina to play with 10 men for 30 minutes in a decision that was completely unfair. American players learned of Balogun's availability when social media posts started popping up during the 10-minute bus ride Sunday morning from their hotel to training at the University of Washington's Husky Soccer Stadium. Balogun, a 25-year-old who plays for Monaco, scored 13 Ligue 1 goals last season and has 12 goals in 30 international appearances.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November for 18th Year
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The event marks nearly two decades of the festival bringing seafood vendors and entertainment to the Vero Beach waterfront. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the annual gathering.

The festival has become a regular autumn attraction for Indian River County residents and visitors. Previous years have drawn crowds for seafood vendors, live music, and family activities along the coast.

Specific dates for the November 2026 festival will be announced by organizers. More information will be available through Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. as the event approaches.

cards.headline: Florida median-income households now need 17 months longer to save for home down payment
cards.teaser: A new study shows that saving for a down payment on a home takes significantly longer for Florida households than it did a decade ago.
cards.body:
A new study by Smart Asset found that it now takes the median-income household earner in Florida 17 months longer to save up for a down payment in 2026 than in 2016. For Floridians who earn a minimum wage of $14 an hour, it takes nearly 26 years to save up for a down payment on a home.

Florida was No. 25 on this list, while residents in Idaho have been affected the most in the last 10 years. Residents of Idaho now need 40 months longer to buy a home than in 2016. Only in three states, Louisiana, Mississippi and North Dakota, can median-income households save a down payment faster than they could in 2016. West Virginia has the nation's lowest down payment burden. A median-income household in West Virginia needs 5.5 years to save for a down payment in 2026, just three months longer than in 2016. According to the study, saving for a down payment on a minimum-wage income alone is essentially impossible in every state.

hero.headline: Vision Marine Technologies to sell Palm City property, consolidates operations
hero.teaser: Vision Marine Technologies has a pending sale of its Palm City property and has consolidated tender-rigging operations at its Fort Lauderdale marina.
hero.body:
Vision Marine Technologies announced the pending sale of its Palm City property. The company has completed consolidating its tender-rigging operations at its Fort Lauderdale marina location.

The consolidation moves tender-rigging work from Palm City to Fort Lauderdale. Vision Marine completed this operational shift as it prepares to sell the Martin County property.

The company announced both the consolidation completion and the pending property sale on Tuesday. The moves represent a restructuring of Vision Marine's Florida operations.

Vision Marine Technologies focuses on marine operations in Florida. The Fort Lauderdale marina location will now serve as the consolidated base for the company's tender-rigging services.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County pancreatic cancer patient approved for experimental treatment after 62-day wait
hero.body:
Russell Reed, a 64-year-old St. Lucie County man battling pancreatic cancer, has been approved to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug his family hopes will give him more time. Reed spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved to receive the treatment after traditional treatments were no longer effective.

Daraxonrasib, also known as RMC-6236, is an investigational once-daily oral pill developed by Revolution Medicines. The drug targets mutated KRAS proteins, which drive more than 90% of pancreatic cancers. While the treatment is not yet FDA-approved, early clinical trial results have generated optimism among some patients and physicians. According to Reed's family, his oncologist submitted a request through the FDA's Expanded Access Program, which can allow patients with serious or life-threatening illnesses to receive treatments outside of clinical trials when other options are limited. "Chemotherapy isn't going to help me at this point," Reed said.

While waiting for an answer, Reed and his wife Marnie focused on making the most of their time together. For Marnie, the fight was never just about accessing a drug. It was about more family trips, more memories and more moments together. "The idea of sitting here and waiting for the phone to ring is not ok with me," Marnie Reed said. "You're still here, and if you don't pay attention, you're going to miss it. I don't want to miss a minute with him." Reed said research and clinical trial results gave him hope that daraxonrasib could help slow the progression of his disease. "There's a lot of anecdotal evidence and a lot of evidence from the clinical trials that show that this is the miracle drug for pancreatic cancer," Reed said. "It is not a cure, but it will give me time."

Reed received approval just two days after sharing his story with WPTV. The drug is now in his hands, and his family says he is already feeling better and optimistic about what comes next. While daraxonrasib is not considered a cure for pancreatic cancer, the Reeds say the approval represents something they have been fighting for all along: more time together.

cards.headline: Construction begins on 18-hole golf course at Esplanade at Solaeris in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Taylor Morrison has started construction on a Wilczynski-designed golf course at its new Esplanade at Solaeris residential community in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Construction has begun on an 18-hole golf course at Esplanade at Solaeris, Taylor Morrison's new golf residential community in Port St. Lucie. The course was designed by Wilczynski.

The Esplanade at Solaeris development represents Taylor Morrison's entry into the Port St. Lucie golf community market. The golf course will serve as the centerpiece of the residential community.

cards.headline: Legacy High School Named New Voting Location for Precinct 90 Voters in Tradition
cards.teaser: Legacy High School will serve as a new voting location for voters in Precinct 90 during the Primary Election on August 18, 2026, according to St. Lucie County Supervisor of Electio
cards.body:
Legacy High School will serve as a new voting location for voters in Precinct 90 during the Primary Election on August 18, 2026, according to St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker.

The school, located at 14505 Crosstown Parkway in Port St. Lucie, will serve voters who live north of Crosstown Parkway in the Tradition area.

Precinct 90 voters previously cast ballots at Tradition Town Hall, which is Precinct 89. Since the 2024 General Election, the voter population in the area has grown, prompting the Supervisor of Elections Office to search for an additional voting site.

Walker said the office worked with the St. Lucie County School District to secure Legacy High School as the new precinct location.

"We are grateful to the School District and Legacy High School for their commitment to serving this community," the Supervisor of Elections Office said.

The office said it is still searching for an Early Voting site to serve Tradition's rapidly growing population. Officials said the addition of Legacy High School as a precinct location is intended to help reduce Election Day wait times and ease pressure on Early Voting at the Paula A. Lewis Library.

Voters in Precinct 90 will receive mailed notifications from the Supervisor of Elections Office about the change to their assigned voting location.

For additional information, voters can contact the St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Office at 772-462-1500 or visit www.stlucievotes.gov.

hero.headline: Vero Beach homeowner faces selling home as insurance costs hit $9,000 per year
hero.body:
A Vero Beach homeowner says rising insurance costs may force her to sell her home within months. Kelly Hagen said her annual homeowners insurance premium has climbed to $9,000, adding $750 per month on top of her mortgage payment for her 1,500-square-foot, three-bedroom, two-bathroom home built in 1994. The premium jumped from $6,000 to $8,000 and then to $9,000 in successive years, leaving her struggling to keep up with the relentless increases.

Hagen's insurance company requires impact windows, an expensive upgrade she has struggled to afford while working two jobs. She works full time and also drives for Instacart during nights and weekends to try to make ends meet. Her situation worsened when she was turned away for a $10,000 My Safe Florida Home grant after it took too long to find a contractor, a roadblock many Florida homeowners have faced. When asked how much longer she could manage the increases, Hagen said probably just a couple more months before she would have to try to sell her house. She said leaving would be devastating.

State leaders are encouraging homeowners to shop around, pointing to new insurers entering the market with competitive rates. Stand Insurance, a new company, is offering to help homeowners connect with affordable contractors using AI technology to study homes and then works to pair homeowners with vendors and contractors to make repairs. CEO Dan Preston said helping homeowners be safer reduces claim payouts and lowers premiums for customers. He explained that if you can actually help someone be safer and have their home be safer, it benefits everyone involved because the company does not have to pay out in claims and customers pay less in premiums.

Experts advise homeowners in similar situations to explore workable changes to their policy and shop around for lower premiums with other insurance companies. For Hagen, the window to find a solution is closing fast as the financial pressure has left her with few options if costs continue to climb. Her story reflects a crisis facing many Florida homeowners who are being priced out of their homes by soaring insurance costs and expensive mitigation requirements they cannot afford to meet.
